title: She wasn’t called “Eve”… until after she fell.
paragraphs: She wasn’t called “Eve”… until after she fell.
Because some of you are still waiting to be “worthy” before you believe God can name you.
But what if I told you…

Her identity didn’t come at her best moment—
It came at her worst?
We’ve been taught to think names come with perfection.

The fruit is already bitten.
The silence of God is already heavy.
The shame is already clinging to their skin like dust and sweat.
That’s where many of us are too.

Smiling in public.
Dying in private.
Compromises we swore we’d never make.
You didn’t plan to fall this far.
And the loudest voice in your head?
But Genesis tells a different story.

Genesis 3:20
“The man called his wife’s name Eve, because she would become the mother of all the living.”
Why not in the beauty of Eden’s perfection?
Because something happened right before that moment.

Genesis 3:15
“He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.”
The first declaration that sin would not have the final word.
Some scholars interpret this as the Protoevangelium—the first announcement of the coming Messiah.
So when he looks at the woman who just participated in humanity’s fall…
He doesn’t label her by her failure.
Her name was not rooted in her mistake.
It was rooted in God’s promise.
Are still answering to names God never gave you.
But heaven is not naming you based on your worst chapter.
Heaven names you based on redemption.
God did not ignore the sin.
“I will deal with it… and then I will redeem you.”
And that redemption has a name.
Where Eve reached for the forbidden…
Jesus was stripped and exposed on a cross.

2 Corinthians 5:21
“God made Him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”
Jesus took the name you deserved…
So you could receive the identity you never earned.
The head of the serpent was crushed.
You don’t have to live under your old name.

2 Corinthians 5:17
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.”
So why are you still introducing yourself by your past?
Why are you still agreeing with shame?
Why are you still hiding when Jesus already exposed Himself for you?
You don’t need to clean yourself up first.
Eve wasn’t named after she fixed everything.
She was named after God promised redemption.
And God is still making that promise today.

Your sin can be forgiven.
Your shame can be lifted.
Your identity can be rewritten.

Romans 10:13
“Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”
What name have you been carrying…
That Jesus is ready to replace?
And receive the name Heaven is speaking over you:
You might be the voice that reminds them…
